summary.body: Northborough, Southborough, and Regional School Committees and Superintendency Union #3
summary.headline: The combined school committees gave the superintendent an exemplary evaluation and approved a 3.5 percent pay raise for 2026-2027.
summary.summary: At a joint session on June 15, 2026, the Northborough, Southborough, Regional, and Superintendency Union #3 school committees reviewed the district's 2025 MetroWest Adolescent Health Survey results and received an update on the draft Vision 2032 strategic plan. Following the presentation of his 2025-2026 summative evaluation with an overall rating of exemplary, the committees convened in executive session to negotiate the superintendent's contract. Upon returning to open session, all committees voted unanimously to approve a 3.5 percent cost-of-living salary increase for Superintendent Greg Martineau for the 2026-2027 school year.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: Superintendency Union #3 elected officers for the upcoming year, and the committees reappointed the district physician and approved meeting minutes from March 11, 2026.
key_details: Chelsea Malinowski was elected chair of Superintendency Union #3, with Laura Kaufman as vice chair and Alan Zelek as secretary.
Dr. Safdar Medina was unanimously reappointed as the school physician for the 2026-2027 school year across all committees.
Joint open session meeting minutes from March 11, 2026 were approved unanimously.
topics.outcome: Officers elected, school physician reappointed, and minutes approved.

topics.title: 2025 MetroWest Adolescent Health Survey results
topics.summary: District staff presented high-level trends from the 2025 MetroWest Adolescent Health Survey covering students at Melican Middle School, Trottier Middle School, and Algonquin Regional High School. The data showed overall regional declines in substance use and bullying, alongside improving protective factors, but highlighted persistent disparities in mental health stress and anxiety among female, LGBTQ+, and minority students, as well as concerns regarding smartphone usage during and outside school.
key_details: Participation included 500 students at Melican (90.6 percent), 386 at Trottier (89.6 percent), and 982 at Algonquin (90.6 percent).
High school substance use in the past 30 days dropped across all categories, including an 11.2 percent decrease in alcohol use.
Middle school reports of high stress and anxiety rose slightly, with higher rates reported among female students, Black students, Hispanic/Latino students, and LGBTQ+ youth.
Over 40 percent of students in middle and high school reported spending three or more hours per day on smartphones outside of school for non-school purposes.
The MetroWest Health Foundation is offering non-competitive implementation grants to participating districts to address survey findings.
topics.outcome: Survey results were reviewed; individual school committees will receive deeper school-specific presentations in the fall.
topics.why_it_matters: The survey data informs district wellness policies, mental health supports, cell phone rules, and community prevention programming affecting local middle and high school students.

topics.title: Policy development and distribution
topics.summary: The committees reviewed a first reading of an updated policy on medication administration in schools to align with state regulation changes, and received distribution copies of five previously approved policies.
key_details: Policy J-220 regarding medication administration in school was updated to comply with amended Massachusetts regulation 105 CMR 210.
The revised medication administration policy will be posted online for public feedback before a second reading in the fall.

Approved policies distributed included Middle School Pathway Exploration, Controversial Issues/Speakers (I-360), School Immunization Requirements (J-120), Wellness Policy (J-320), and Athletic Concussion Policy (J-340).
topics.outcome: Policy J-220 was received for a first reading; approved policies were formally distributed.

topics.title: Strategic plan reauthorization: Vision 2032 update
topics.summary: Superintendent Greg Martineau presented a progress report on the draft Vision 2032 strategic plan, which builds on the previous Vision 2026 framework. The updated plan places special emphasis on future readiness, ethical integration of artificial intelligence and emerging technology, student voice, and belonging across five core strategic objectives.
key_details: The plan retains five strategic objectives: empowering learners, belonging, opportunity and student success, healthy and balanced learners, educator learning and leadership, and finance and operations.
New elements focus on preparing students for changing workforce demands and the responsible use of artificial intelligence.
A formal presentation with implementation action steps, timelines, and measurable performance indicators will be delivered in September.
topics.outcome: Information presented; the final plan and action roadmap will be brought forward in fall 2026.

topics.title: District personnel updates
topics.summary: The superintendent announced key administrative transitions across Northborough and Southborough schools heading into the 2026-2027 school year.
key_details: Helene Desjardins is concluding her district service at the end of June.
Deb Lemieux will assume the role of principal at Finn School in Southborough.
Jessica Burke starts July 1 as director of student services for Northborough.
Contract negotiations are finalizing for Dan Meiser to serve as director of student services for Southborough starting in July.

topics.title: Superintendent 2025-2026 summative evaluation
topics.summary: The committees presented the 2025-2026 summative evaluation for Superintendent Greg Martineau, incorporating feedback from all 19 sitting committee members. Martineau received an overall rating of exemplary, earning praise for curriculum consistency across three districts, passing balanced level-service budgets, facility project oversight, and active community visibility.
key_details: Martineau received an exemplary rating across all four standards: Instructional Leadership, Management and Operations, Family and Community Engagement, and Professional Culture.
Family and community engagement saw the highest individual marks, with nearly 79 percent of members rating his performance exemplary.
Commended accomplishments included launching new math curricula, managing administrative transitions, and securing town meeting budget approvals in both towns.
Identified areas for continuing focus included tracking high school math rollouts, managing aging school facilities, and monitoring middle school mental health trends.
topics.outcome: The summative evaluation was unanimously approved as presented by all four bodies.

topics.title: Superintendent contract and 2026-2027 salary increase
topics.summary: Following an executive session for contract negotiations, the committees returned to open session and voted to award Superintendent Greg Martineau a cost-of-living salary increase for the 2026-2027 school year.
key_details: The voted increase applies a 3.5 percent cost-of-living adjustment to Martineau's existing salary of $239,095.
The new total annual salary is set at $247,463.33 for the 2026-2027 school year.
The motion was approved unanimously by roll call or voice vote across Northborough, Southborough, Regional, and Union #3 committees.
topics.why_it_matters: Sets executive administrative compensation funded across both town school budgets and the regional high school district.
